c.tagline: Aegean island of mastic villages, medieval mansions, and quiet beaches.

taxi.fareNote: No Uber or ride-hailing apps operate on Chios; taxis are hailed, taken from a rank, or booked by phone. Fares are metered, but agreeing a price up front for longer trips across the island is common.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number reaching police, fire, and ambulance; the coast guard is 108.

hood_desc: The island capital and main port, wrapped around a Genoese-era castle and a lively seafront of cafes and tavernas; the most convenient, walkable base for first-timers.
A fragrant plain of high-walled 14th-19th-century citrus estates and stone mansions just south of town; atmospheric and quiet, best for travelers wanting character and calm over nightlife.
The island's main beach-resort strip a few kilometres south of Chios Town, with a sandy bay, hotels, and seasonal tavernas; an easy base for a beach-focused stay.

The medieval mastic-producing villages of southern Chios - Mesta's labyrinth of fortified alleys and Pyrgi's black-and-white 'xysta' geometric facades; steeped in history and best for slow, atmospheric days.
A striking hilltop village in the rugged northwest crowned by a Byzantine-Genoese castle, ringed by quiet beaches and restored stone houses; a romantic, off-the-beaten-path base.

water.note: Tap water in Chios Town is generally drinkable, but many locals and visitors prefer bottled.

sys.n: KTEL Chios (blue urban & green intercity buses)

transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the driver or conductor (roughly 1.80-5 EUR by distance); there is no rechargeable transit card. Blue city buses serve Chios Town and its suburbs, while green KTEL buses reach the mastic villages and the north a few times a day.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am-9pm with reduced weekend and off-season service and no night buses, so taxis fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Chios has no metro, tram, or rail; the blue/green KTEL bus network plus taxis and rental cars are how you get around, and a car is strongly recommended for reaching remote beaches and villages.

ferry: Port of Chios (ferries to Piraeus, Lesvos, Samos, and Çeşme, Turkey)

transit.m: Local blue bus on the nearby main road (limited)

tip.r: A service charge is often included; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Mesta
A perfectly preserved medieval labyrinth built by the Genoese, its vaulted stone alleys spiral inward to the grand Taxiarches church at the fortified core.
Chios Castle and Kastro quarter
The Byzantine-Genoese fortress enclosing the old Turkish and Jewish quarters of Chios Town still shelters lived-in lanes, mosques, and crumbling seaward bastions.
Chios Mastic Museum
Set among mastic groves near Pyrgi, this sleek museum unravels the story of the island's UNESCO-recognized mastic cultivation, a resin grown nowhere else on earth.
Kampos district
An aristocratic quarter of walled Genoese citrus estates south of town, its ochre stone mansions, pergolas, and orange-scented lanes evoke centuries of merchant wealth.
Daskalopetra (Teacher's Rock)
Legend holds Homer taught his pupils from this carved stone throne above Vrontados bay, a simple, evocative shrine to the island's claimed native poet.
Mavra Volia beach
Near Emporios, volcanic black pebbles shelve into deep sapphire water at this striking crescent cove, the mastic coast's most dramatic swimming spot.
Korais Library and Argenti Museum
One of Greece's oldest libraries houses 135,000 rare volumes alongside the Argenti folklore collection, chronicling Chian costume, genealogy, and island history.
Chios Archaeological Museum
A museum near the port displaying finds from prehistoric, classical and Byzantine sites across the island, including sculpture, pottery and inscribed stelae.
Chios Maritime Museum
A neoclassical mansion on Aplotaria Street devoted to the island's long seafaring tradition, filled with ship models, nautical instruments and maritime paintings.
Giustiniani Palace Museum
A 14th-century fortress built into the Kastro's walls, once the Genoese governor's seat, now displaying Byzantine and Genoese sculpture near the old town's main square.

bus.note: KTEL Chios green buses connect Chios Town with the mastic villages (Mesta, Pyrgi, Olympi), Volissos, and northern villages; there are no international bus routes (Chios is an island).

intl.to: Çeşme, Turkey (seasonal ~30-45 min crossing, mainly summer)

ferry.note: Chios's port links to Piraeus/Athens on overnight ferries (~7-9 hrs, operators Blue Star Ferries and Hellenic Seaways), plus Lesvos and Samos in the North Aegean; a seasonal international line crosses to Çeşme, Turkey.

half.name: Nea Moni Monastery
half.blurb: 11th-century UNESCO-listed monastery in the mountainous interior, famed for its Byzantine mosaics.

half.name: Pyrgi & the Mastic Villages
half.blurb: Medieval villages of southern Chios with Pyrgi's geometric 'xysta' facades and fortified Mesta.

half.name: Anavatos
half.blurb: A dramatic abandoned 'ghost' village clinging to a cliff, sometimes called the Mystras of the Aegean.

full.name: Oinousses
full.blurb: A small shipowners' island a short ferry from Chios, with quiet beaches and a maritime museum.

full.name: Psara
full.blurb: Remote, history-steeped island northwest of Chios, known for its role in the Greek War of Independence.

full.name: Çeşme, Turkey
full.blurb: Turkish resort town reachable by seasonal ferry, with a seafront castle and thermal spas.
